name: r5-account
statement: On MATH-500 at AI2's setting (T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, one sample each), the 65 problems that Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math gets right and the cued Olmo 3 base gets wrong break down into four mechanisms and a small remainder. (1) Budget: about 0.25 are problems where the cued base ran to the 16,384-token cap without a loop. These are long problems on which the base keeps going and never commits, while RL, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, finishes. (2) Answer statement: about 0.15 are problems where the base's failure was in stating the answer: a right value in a rejected or garbled final line, or a reached gold that it then overwrote. (3) Reliability: about 0.51 are problems the base solves in at least one of four other independent samples. The miss here is a sample-specific slip or misread on a problem the base can do, and RL removes it by concentrating on paths the base already samples. This is the largest part and the one still open. (4) Capability: about 0.07 are problems the base never solves in four further samples while RL solves at least two of four. Here RL uses a plan the base does not sample. (Unassigned) About 0.02 are problems where RL's single right answer was itself a lucky draw: RL is right in at most one of four other samples.
gap: Cells: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json, T1 = base Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token opening cue and T2 = Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math with the plain prompt, both MATH-500 (500 problems), T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, max 16,384 new tokens, 1 sample, grader v3 (fields t1_right, t2_right). A gap problem is a row with t2_right true and t1_right false (cell rl_only). Cap hits count as wrong through their stored t1_right/t2_right, and a row with t1_right or t2_right null or missing is not a gap problem. Expected size is 65 problems (result-5e17a6). The rules also read the independent 4-sample rows of the same two models at the same setting: D = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and E = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl, attempt == 0, samples 0-3. kB and kR are the numbers of those rows with score_v3 == 1. Cap-hit rows, null score_v3 and missing samples count as wrong, and a duplicated (problem_index, sample) uses its first row in file order.

parts.name: budget
parts.mechanism: The cued base keeps writing past the 16,384-token budget without committing on long problems (no rule-A loop at T 1.0), while RL, trained with truncated rollouts as negatives, finishes. This revives the termination idea of r1-across-2 and r1-surprises-1, which were refuted on weight-dose answer counts (theta 1.5 word salad) and on a hard328 pass@4 count, not on which stored problems hit the cap, so their refuting tests do not apply to this per-problem rule.
parts.rule: per_problem.json row of the problem has t1_cap_hit == true.

parts.name: answer-statement
parts.mechanism: The base reaches the right value but fails at stating it: a final line that v3 rejects or that is garbled, or a gold value overwritten by a later answer marker (the untested r4-m11/r4-m12 mechanisms, not refuted). RL boxes once and stops.
parts.rule: Not taken by an earlier rule, and the per_problem.json field failure_type, lower-cased, contains at least one of the substrings 'format', 'final line', 'garbled', 'rejected', 'changed'. A null or missing failure_type is not taken.

parts.name: reliability
parts.mechanism: The base can solve the problem, and the T1 miss is a sample-specific slip or misread. RL sharpens the base's own distribution onto paths it already samples. This revives the slip-removal readings of r2-revise-2 and r3-surprises-1. Their refuting tests were a hard328 vote@4 count and a vote tie-break count, which make claims about vote procedures, not about whether the base solves a gap problem in independent samples, so they do not apply here.
parts.rule: Not taken by an earlier rule, and kB >= 1 (at least one of the 4 attempt-0 base_cue rows in D with score_v3 == 1).

parts.name: capability
parts.mechanism: RL uses a plan the base does not sample on this problem: the base fails all four independent samples, while RL solves the problem repeatedly.
parts.rule: Not taken by an earlier rule, and kB == 0 and kR >= 2 (at least two of the 4 attempt-0 RL rows in E with score_v3 == 1).

scope: Covers the 65 RL-only problems of the stored MATH-500 T1/T2 pair at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, grader v3, one sample per model. It does not cover the 12 base-only problems (the gap counted here is gross, not net), T 0.6 cells (where loops dominate), the hard328 set, the Code pair or 3.0 checkpoints. Part 2 rests on one reader's hand label (failure_type). Parts 3-4 classify with 4 further samples per model, so a problem with a base rate near 0.1 can fall into capability by chance.

imports.finding: RLVR raises pass@1 by concentrating on paths the base model already samples. Per-problem MATH-500 coverage at 128 samples is almost the same for both models.
imports.how: Grounds the reliability part: on most gap problems the base's own samples already contain the right path, so RL's gain there is concentration, not new reach.

imports.finding: Rule-based math verifiers miss correctly formatted variants (average recall 86 %).
imports.how: Grounds the answer-statement part: some base gap misses are right values in forms the rule-based v3 rejects.

imports.finding: In Olmo 3, RL-Zero-Math multiplies an existing 'wait' marker. At T 0.6 RL hits the length limit more often than the base.
imports.how: Places the budget part in termination policy rather than skill: RL changes when the model keeps checking and when it stops.

explains.quote: 16 cap hits with no loop, 14 misread
explains.how: The budget part is exactly the T1 cap hits among the 65, so its predicted share is 16/65.

explains.quote: 8 right answer in a rejected or garbled final line
explains.how: Together with the 2 'reached gold then changed it' labels, these make up the answer-statement part (about 10 of 65).
A fresh base sample solves most gap problems, which is what the large reliability part says.
Base-0/4 problems fail by wrong plan, which matches the separate, small capability part.

explains.quote: sits in problems the base solves at least once in 4
explains.how: The gap sits mainly where the base sometimes succeeds, i.e. in the reliability part.

explains.quote: At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3
explains.how: The budget part is non-loop overrun at T 1.0, not the T 0.6 loop mechanism.
Budget problems are long problems that also cap or fail on a restart, so restarts recover only a small fraction of the budget part.

conflicts.quote: turn 10 of the base's 2,000 samples right and 0 of RL's
conflicts.how: Label-free extraction rules repair only 0.5 points, which is less than a 0.15 answer-statement share suggests. Either the hand label overstates format failures, or many of them are forms (garbled lines, overwritten gold) that no extraction rule can repair.

rival: The strongest rival is a pure sampling-noise budget: every gap problem is a draw from the base's per-problem success rate, so cap hits and answer-statement misses are just ways a sample fails and are not separate mechanisms. Under it, the cap-hit gap problems behave like the rest: the random matched-norm cell (a fresh base sample) solves them at about the overall 40/65 = 0.62 rate, and their other base samples cap no more often than base samples in general. This account instead predicts that the random cell solves only about 0.35 of the budget problems and that about 0.75 of them have at least one other cap hit in D. The random-cell solve rate on the budget part is the number that separates the two (0.35 here against about 0.6 under the rival).

predictions.experiment: Base-only intervention aimed at the reliability part: Olmo-3-1025-7B base with the 3-token cue [1584, 2268, 33413], MATH-500 all 500 problems, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, max 16,384 new tokens, one new sample per problem (seed 5,000,000 + problem_index, no restarts), then a majority vote over 5 answers per problem: the 4 attempt-0 samples of studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl plus the new sample. Votes are cast by the extracted_v3 of finished answers, whitespace removed (cap hits and empty answers cast no vote). Ties go to the answer of the shortest finished tied sample (fewest n_new). The chosen answer is graded with v3; a problem with no vote counts as wrong.
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 445 or more than 459 right of 500
